title: "Methods"

```{r}
suppressMessages({library(readr); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(knitr)})
rd  <- function(f) read_csv(file.path("data", f), show_col_types=FALSE)
pct <- function(x) paste0(round(100*x), "%")
num <- function(x, d=1) ifelse(is.na(x), "–", formatC(x, format="f", digits=d))
sgn <- function(x, d=1) ifelse(is.na(x), "–", sprintf(paste0("%+.", d, "f"), x))
ci  <- function(lo, hi, d=1) ifelse(is.na(lo), "–", paste0("[", num(lo, d), ", ", num(hi, d), "]"))
pv  <- function(p) ifelse(is.na(p), "–", ifelse(p < 0.001, "< 0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p)))
journal.order <- c("AER","AER:Insights","AEA P&P","AEJ:Applied Economics","AEJ:Economic Policy",
                   "AEJ:Macro","AEJ:Micro","JEL","JEP","Main journals","All journals")
```

## Methods in brief

- **Journals:** the main analysis covers the AER, AER:Insights and the four AEJs ("main journals"). The AEA P&P, JEL and JEP are reported on the [Appendix](appendix.qmd) page.
- **Articles:** research articles come from Crossref. Front matter, book reviews, editorial and administrative items, and comments, replies and errata are dropped. Before 2018, the Papers and Proceedings (P&P) appeared as the May issue of the AER; here they are counted as AEA P&P.
- **Packages:** a package is an openICPSR project. It is matched to an article through the migration of historical supplements, a DataCite link, a citation in the article's reference list, or a deposit titled "Data and Code for: *article title*".
- **Time from submission to publication:** the submission year and manuscript number come from manuscript-number DOIs (since 2015). The quartiles of the manuscript numbers give the submission quarter. Publication is the month of the print issue.
- **Years:** unless stated otherwise, years are years of print publication. Tables cover complete years only.
- **Article-level data:** every article, with the flags used here and the DOIs of its packages, is on the [Data](data.qmd) page.

## Replication packages

**Table 1. Share of research articles with a replication package, by policy period, main journals**

```{r}
rd("packages_by_period_site.csv") %>% filter(!appendix) %>%
  mutate(group=factor(group, levels=journal.order)) %>% arrange(group, period) %>%
  transmute(Group=group, Period=period, Years=paste0(first_year,"–",last_year),
            Articles=articles, `With a package`=articles_with_package, Share=pct(share)) %>%
  kable(align="lllrrr")
```

**Table 2. Research articles with a replication package, by year, main journals (AER, AER:Insights, AEJs)**

```{r}
rd("share_by_journal_year.csv") %>%
  filter(Journal=="Main journals") %>%
  transmute(Year=as.character(year), Articles=articles, `With a package`=with_package, Share=pct(share)) %>%
  kable(align="lrrr")
```

## Time from submission to publication

Months, by journal. The P&P, JEL and JEP are not included (no submission-based manuscript numbers). Before and after are defined by **year of publication** (published before 2019 vs. published 2019 and later), not by submission year.

**Table 3. Articles published before 2019 vs. published 2019 and later**

The shift is the Hodges–Lehmann estimate (after minus before). The mean difference has a Welch 95% confidence interval. p-values are from the Wilcoxon rank-sum test, Holm-adjusted across journals. Cutoff: year of publication (2019; 2020 as a robustness check). "Before" means published before the cutoff year, "after" published in it or later.

```{r}
rd("time_to_pub_tests.csv") %>%
  mutate(Journal=factor(Journal, levels=journal.order)) %>% arrange(cutoff, Journal) %>%
  transmute(Cutoff=as.character(cutoff), Journal, `n before`=n_pre, `n after`=n_post,
            `Median before`=num(median_pre, 0), `Median after`=num(median_post, 0),
            Shift=sgn(shift, 0), `Mean difference`=sgn(mean_diff), `95% CI`=ci(mean_diff_lo, mean_diff_hi),
            `p (Holm)`=pv(p_wilcox_holm)) %>%
  kable(align="llrrrrrrrr")
```

**Table 4. Articles with and without a replication package**

Differences are "with" minus "without". Statistics are as in Table 3. Articles without a package include those exempt from the policy (no data or code) and those whose package was not matched.

```{r}
rd("time_to_pub_by_package.csv") %>%
  mutate(Journal=factor(Journal, levels=journal.order)) %>% arrange(Journal) %>%
  transmute(Journal, Period=period, `n with`=n_package, `n without`=n_no_package,
            `Median with`=num(median_package, 0), `Median without`=num(median_no_package, 0),
            `Mean difference`=sgn(mean_diff), `95% CI`=ci(mean_diff_lo, mean_diff_hi),
            `p (Holm)`=pv(p_wilcox_holm)) %>%
  kable(align="llrrrrrrr")
```

**Table 5. Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests: are the two distributions different?**

*D* is the largest gap between the two empirical cumulative distributions. Each distribution is a set of shares, so groups of different sizes are comparable. The sizes enter through the effective sample size *n*₁*n*₂/(*n*₁+*n*₂): the 5% critical value is 1.358/√*n*~eff~. Times fall on a grid and have many ties, which makes the asymptotic p-value conservative. The permutation p-value comes from 10,000 reshuffles of the group labels, keeping both group sizes. It is exact for the observed sizes and ties, and is Holm-adjusted across journals within each comparison and period. Groups with fewer than 5 articles are not tested.

```{r}
rd("time_to_pub_ks.csv") %>%
  mutate(Journal=factor(Journal, levels=journal.order)) %>% arrange(comparison, Journal, period) %>%
  transmute(Comparison=comparison, Journal, Period=period, n1, n2, `n eff`=num(n_eff, 0),
            D=num(D, 3), `5% critical D`=num(D_crit_5, 3), `p asymptotic`=pv(p_asymptotic),
            `p permutation (Holm)`=pv(p_permutation_holm),
            Different=ifelse(is.na(D), "–", ifelse(significant, "yes", "no"))) %>%
  kable(align="lllrrrrrrrl")
```

## Policy regressions

### Event study (main specification) {#event-study}

For each outcome $y$, on articles in the AER and the four AEJs published 2015 to the latest complete year (AER:Insights has no years before 2019):

$$y_{ijt} = \alpha_j + f_j(q_i) + \sum_{k \neq 2018} \beta_k \, \mathbb{1}(t = k) + \varepsilon_{ijt},$$

with $q_i$ counted from the first quarter of 2019. All main journals are covered from 2019, so calendar-year effects cannot be estimated separately from $\beta_k$; instead, $f_j$ is one of:

- **None:** $f_j = 0$. Estimated by OLS with journal fixed effects; $\beta_k$ is the within-journal mean in year $k$ minus the mean in 2018.
- **Linear, quadratic:** $f_j(q) = \delta_j q$ or $\delta_j q + \gamma_j q^2$, estimated with $\alpha_j$ on the articles published 2015–2018 only, then extrapolated. $\beta_k$ is the mean of $y - \hat\alpha_j - \hat f_j(q_i)$ in year $k$ minus that in 2018.
- **Rolling:** for each year $k$, $\alpha_j + \delta_j q$ is estimated on years $k-3$ to $k-1$, and $\beta_k$ is the mean of $y - \hat\alpha_j - \hat\delta_j q_i$ in year $k$. There is no reference year.

A journal enters a trend version only with at least three years in the window used to fit the trend: for the time to publication, the AER (2018 only before the policy) is in the no-trend version only, and the rolling version starts in 2019. Confidence intervals are 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles of 499 bootstrap draws that resample journal issues within journal and year, re-estimating the trend in each draw; p-values are twice the share of draws on the other side of zero.

**Table E1. Event study, main journals pooled**

Each cell: estimate, then the 95% bootstrap confidence interval. Packages in percentage points, time to publication in months. – : reference year, or not estimated.

```{r}
es <- rd("event_study.csv")
trend.lab <- c(none="No trend", linear="Linear trend", quadratic="Quadratic trend", rolling="Rolling trend")
es %>% filter(Journal=="Main journals") %>%
  mutate(scale=if_else(outcome=="has_package", 100, 1),
         Outcome=if_else(outcome=="has_package", "Replication package (pp)", "Time to publication (months)"),
         Trend=factor(trend.lab[trend], levels=trend.lab),
         value=if_else(is.na(se) & trend != "rolling", "0 (ref.)",
                       paste0(sgn(scale*estimate), ifelse(!is.na(p) & p < 0.05, "*", ""), " ", ci(scale*lo, scale*hi)))) %>%
  select(Outcome, Trend, year, value) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from=year, values_from=value, values_fill="–") %>%
  arrange(Outcome, Trend) %>%
  select(Outcome, Trend, all_of(as.character(sort(unique(es$year))))) %>%
  kable()
```

### Static regressions (robustness) {#regression-equations}

All models are estimated by OLS at the article level. For (a), each model is also estimated as a probit (see below). Standard errors are clustered by journal × year of publication (CR1, with *G* − 1 degrees of freedom).

**Notation**

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $i$ | article |
| $j$ | journal the article is attributed to (P&P articles printed in the May AER through 2017 count as AEA P&P) |
| $t$ | **year of print publication** of article $i$ |
| $c$ | cutoff year: 2019 (actual) or 2017, 2018, 2020, 2021 (placebos) |
| $q_{i}$ | **publication quarter** of article $i$ (from the month of the print issue), counted from the first quarter of year $c$: $q_i = 4\,(t - c) + (\text{quarter}_i - 1)$. So $q_i = 0$ for January–March of year $c$, $-1$ for October–December of year $c-1$. |
| $y_{ijt}$ | outcome: (a) $\text{Pkg}_{i}$, or (b) $\text{Months}_{i}$ |
| $\text{Pkg}_{i}$ | 1 if article $i$ has a replication package in the AEA Data and Code Repository, 0 otherwise. In (a) it is the outcome (linear probability model); in (b) it is a regressor. |
| $\text{Months}_{i}$ | months from the middle of the submission quarter to the month of the print issue |
| $\text{Post}^{c}_{t}$ | **1 if the article was published in year $c$ or later**, i.e. $\mathbb{1}[t \geq c]$; 0 otherwise. With $c = 2019$: published in 2019 or later. It does not depend on when the article was submitted or accepted. |
| $\text{New}_{j}$ | 1 for journals with no data policy before 2019 (AEA P&P, JEL, JEP); 0 for the AER (policy since 2005) and AEJs (since 2009) |
| $\alpha_j$ | journal fixed effect |
| $\lambda_t$ | publication-year fixed effect |
| $q_{i}$ (as a regressor) | linear trend in publication quarter, centered on the first quarter of the cutoff year, so that $\beta$ is the level shift at $c$ |
| $\varepsilon_{ijt}$ | error term |

The coefficient reported for each model is $\beta$.

**Table 6. Specifications**

| Label | Equation | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Journal FE | (1) $\; y_{ijt} = \alpha_j + \beta\, \text{Post}^{c}_{t} + \varepsilon_{ijt}$ | (a), (b); main journals pooled |
| Journal FE + journal quarterly trends | (2) $\; y_{ijt} = \alpha_j + \delta_j\,q_{i} + \beta\, \text{Post}^{c}_{t} + \varepsilon_{ijt}$ | (a), (b); main journals pooled |
| DiD (year FE) | (3) $\; y_{ijt} = \alpha_j + \lambda_t + \beta\, (\text{Post}^{c}_{t} \times \text{New}_j) + \varepsilon_{ijt}$ | (a); [Appendix](appendix.qmd): AER, AEJs, P&P, JEL, JEP |
| DiD + group quarterly trends | (4) $\; y_{ijt} = \alpha_j + \lambda_t + \theta\, \text{New}_j\,q_{i} + \beta\, (\text{Post}^{c}_{t} \times \text{New}_j) + \varepsilon_{ijt}$ | (a); pooled, AER:Insights excluded |
| Post × has package | (5) $\; \text{Months}_{i} = \alpha_j + \pi\, \text{Post}^{c}_{t} + \gamma\, \text{Pkg}_i + \beta\, (\text{Post}^{c}_{t} \times \text{Pkg}_i) + \varepsilon_{ijt}$ | (b); pooled |
| Before/after (no trend) | (6) $\; y_{it} = \alpha + \beta\, \text{Post}^{c}_{t} + \varepsilon_{it}$ | (a), (b); one journal at a time |
| Before/after + quarterly trend | (7) $\; y_{it} = \alpha + \delta\,q_{i} + \beta\, \text{Post}^{c}_{t} + \varepsilon_{it}$ | (a), (b); one journal at a time |

How to read the coefficients:

- **(1), (2), (6), (7):** $\beta$ is the change in the outcome for articles published from year $c$ on, relative to articles published before. In (2) and (7), this is relative to the journal's own linear trend in publication quarter. In (6) and (7), with a single journal, the journal fixed effect is just the intercept $\alpha$, so (6) is the difference in means.
- **(3), (4):** $\beta$ is the change for newly covered journals (P&P, JEL, JEP), relative to the change in the AER and AEJs in the same publication year. In (4), the common trend is absorbed by $\lambda_t$, and $\theta$ allows the newly covered journals their own trend.
- **(5):** $\pi$ is the change for articles without a package, and $\beta$ is how much more (or less) the time to publication changed for articles with one.

**Probit, for (a).** Equations (1)–(4), (6) and (7) are also estimated as probits, $\Pr(\text{Pkg}_i = 1) = \Phi(x_i'b)$, where $x_i'b$ is the right-hand side of the equation without $\varepsilon$. A probit coefficient is not a change in probability, so the reported effect is

$$\hat\Delta = \frac{1}{N_1} \sum_{i:\, D_i = 1} \left[\Phi(x_i'\hat b) - \Phi(x_i'\hat b - \hat\beta)\right],$$

where $D_i$ is the policy term ($\text{Post}^{c}_t$, or $\text{Post}^{c}_t \times \text{New}_j$ in the DiD) and $N_1$ the number of articles with $D_i = 1$. It is the average change in the probability of having a package for the articles exposed to the (actual or placebo) policy, in percentage points, comparable to $\beta$ from the linear probability model. Its standard error uses the delta method with the same cluster-robust covariance. A journal whose outcome does not vary in the sample (for example, no packages at all) is perfectly predicted by its fixed effect and is dropped. For a single journal, the probit is not estimated when the outcome is constant before or after the cutoff; those cells are missing in Table 9 and in the figure.

**Samples.**
- **Actual cutoff ($c = 2019$):** all years.
- **Actual cutoff, matched window:** the same number of years before and after 2019: 2015–2022 for (a), 2016–2021 for (b) (the first year with submission dates; for the AER, 2018–2021).
- **Placebo cutoffs $c = 2017, 2018$:** articles published before 2019 only.
- **Placebo cutoffs $c = 2020, 2021$:** articles published in 2019 or later only.
- **(a):** articles published 2010 to the latest complete year. Equations (1), (2), (6), (7): main journals (P&P, JEL and JEP in the Appendix). Equations (3), (4): AER, AEJs, P&P, JEL and JEP; AER:Insights, which has no years before 2019, is excluded.
- **(b):** articles in the time-to-publication sample (AER, AER:Insights, AEJs; publication years in which submission quarters can be assigned, 2016–2024 depending on the journal).

```{r}
spec.labels <- c(its_fe="(1) Journal FE", its_trend="(2) Journal FE + journal quarterly trends",
                 did="(3) DiD (year FE)", did_trend="(4) DiD + group quarterly trends", pkg="(5) Post x has package")
spec.single <- c(its_fe="(6) Before/after (no trend)", its_trend="(7) Before/after + quarterly trend")
cell <- function(est, lo, hi, p, scale=1)
  paste0(sgn(scale*est), ifelse(p < 0.05, "*", ""), " ", ci(scale*lo, scale*hi))
pooled_table <- function(r, scale=1) {
  r %>% filter(Journal=="Main journals") %>%
    mutate(Specification=factor(spec.labels[spec], levels=spec.labels),
           value=cell(estimate, lo, hi, p, scale)) %>%
    mutate(col=if_else(type=="actual (matched window)", "2019m", as.character(cutoff))) %>%
    select(any_of("method"), Specification, col, value) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from=col, values_from=value) %>%
    arrange(across(any_of("method")), Specification) %>%
    select(any_of(c(Method="method")), Specification, `2017`, `2018`, `2019`, `2019m`, `2020`, `2021`) %>%
    rename(`Published ≥ 2017 (placebo)`=`2017`, `Published ≥ 2018 (placebo)`=`2018`,
           `Published ≥ 2019 (actual)`=`2019`, `Published ≥ 2019 (actual, matched window)`=`2019m`,
           `Published ≥ 2020 (placebo)`=`2020`, `Published ≥ 2021 (placebo)`=`2021`)
}
journal_table <- function(r, scale=1) {
  r %>% filter(Journal %in% journal.order[1:7], !Journal %in% c("AEA P&P","JEL","JEP")) %>%
    mutate(Journal=factor(Journal, levels=journal.order),
           Specification=factor(spec.single[spec], levels=spec.single)) %>%
    arrange(across(any_of("method")), Journal, Specification, cutoff) %>%
    transmute(across(any_of(c(Method="method"))), Journal, Specification,
              `Cutoff c (published ≥ c)`=paste0(cutoff, case_when(type=="actual" ~ " (actual)", type=="actual (matched window)" ~ " (actual, matched window)", TRUE ~ " (placebo)")),
              Sample=paste0(first_year, "–", last_year), n, Clusters=n_clusters,
              `Mean before`=num(scale*mean_pre), Estimate=sgn(scale*estimate),
              `95% CI`=ci(scale*lo, scale*hi), p=pv(p))
}
reg.pkg   <- rd("regressions_packages.csv") %>% mutate(method=if_else(method=="Probit", "Probit (average effect)", "Linear probability"))
reg.delay <- rd("regressions_time_to_pub.csv") %>% select(-method)
```

**Table 7. Replication package, main journals pooled (percentage points)**

Linear probability model: coefficient $\beta$ from equations (1) and (2) (the difference in differences, (3) and (4), is in Table A2 on the [Appendix](appendix.qmd)). Probit: average effect $\hat\Delta$ from the probit versions of the same equations. Columns are the cutoff $c$: $\text{Post}^{c}_t = 1$ for articles published in year $c$ or later. $c = 2019$ is the actual policy; the other columns are placebos. Each cell shows the estimate, then the 95% confidence interval. \* marks p < 0.05.

```{r}
kable(pooled_table(reg.pkg, scale=100))
```

**Table 8. Time from submission to publication, main journals pooled (months)**

Coefficient $\beta$ from equations (1), (2) and (5); otherwise as Table 7.

```{r}
kable(pooled_table(reg.delay))
```
